title: Strict local invariant description of a finite group quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$. Suppose $q:X\to Y$ is a finite surjective scheme quotient, with orbit-space topology and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$. Let $M$ be an fs log structure on $X$, preserved by $G$, and put $N=(q_*M)^G$, as a sheaf on the small etale site of $Y$. Then $Y$ is Noetherian and the geometric fibres of $q$ are the $G$-orbits. For a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, put $\bar y=q(\bar x)$, $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. The canonical map identifies $B$ with $A^H$, makes $A$ a finite $B$-algebra, and identifies $N_{\bar y}$ with $M_{\bar x}^H$, compatibly with structural maps to $B\hookrightarrow A$. These identifications respect the unit subgroups. Strict local rings and geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; finite means module-finite on affine opens [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; fs log structures are as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. No log regularity, triviality of the action on strata, or generic freeness is assumed.
